name: Malpua
subtitle: fennel-scented pancakes fried in ghee and steeped in cardamom syrup

ingredients.note: gives the chewy centre; at a pinch use 4 tbsp milk powder
the flavour that makes it Rajasthani rather than generic
ghee, not oil — the flavour of the fat is most of the dish

prepNotes: Rest the batter 45 minutes at room temperature. It hydrates the khoya and gives the malpua their chew.
Make the syrup first and keep it warm on the lowest flame. Malpuas go into warm syrup straight from the pan.
The batter should pour off a ladle in a steady ribbon — thicker than a crepe batter, thinner than pancake batter.

steps.text: Boil the sugar and water 5-6 minutes to a sticky syrup just short of one string, add the saffron and cardamom, and keep warm.
steps.tip: A thick syrup will not soak in; too thin and the malpua go soggy. It should feel tacky between the fingers.

steps.text: Mash the grated khoya with 4 tbsp of the milk until lump-free.
Whisk in the maida, rava and crushed fennel, then the rest of the milk, a little at a time, into a smooth pouring batter.
Rest the batter 45 minutes, then check it — it should coat a spoon and drip in a ribbon. Loosen with milk if needed.
Heat 2cm of ghee in a shallow kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter sizzles immediately.
Pour a small ladleful into the centre of the pan. Do not spread it — let it settle into a 8cm disc with frilled edges.
steps.tip: Spreading it tears the malpua. Let the ghee do the work.

steps.text: Fry 2 minutes, spooning hot ghee over the top, until the edges are deep gold and lacy, then flip and fry 1 minute more.
Lift out, drain for a few seconds, and drop straight into the warm syrup. Soak 3-4 minutes, then lift onto a plate.
steps.tip: Longer than 5 minutes and they turn to mush.

steps.text: Repeat with the rest of the batter, frying two at a time, and serve warm with rabri or on their own.

storage: Best warm, within a few hours. Keeps 2 days refrigerated in a little syrup; warm through in a pan or a low oven — the microwave makes them rubbery.
